abstract: |
  A full-sided Mahjong wait has a unique decomposition into a bounded full
  core and freely added triplets at designated coordinates. At each fixed
  order this gives an exact finite sum for every meld-count coefficient,
  a rational ordinary generating series, and a rational-coefficient counting
  polynomial valid from two melds at order one and from $5n-4$ at higher
  orders. Its degree is exactly
  $3n-1$, with leading coefficient $3^{3n-1}/(3n-1)!$. The structural
  decomposition, counting identities, leading term, and exact starting index
  criterion are checked in Lean.
  The resulting density of full waits among uniformly sampled uncapped
  multiplicity vectors tends to one as the meld count increases.

## Finite data for all meld counts {#sec-question}

Use the model of @xue-zhong-2026. There are $3n$ labelled ranks, and a
full-sided $(n,m)$-wait is a nonnegative multiplicity vector of size $3m+1$
that wins after every draw. Melds are triplets or three consecutive ranks.
Fix $n\ge1$, and let $F_n(m)$ count these hands without a physical copy cap.

Adding any triplet preserves full-sidedness. A local version of the
removable-triplet argument in the proof of Proposition 6.8 of
@xue-zhong-2026 uses the abundance profile from Proposition 6.2:

$$
h=\begin{cases}
(2,4,2),&n=1,\\
(2,4,6,\ldots,6,4,2),&n\ge2.
\end{cases}
$$

A canonical sequence hand uses at most $h_i$ tiles at rank $i$.
Consequently, whenever $c_i\ge h_i+3$, each winning draw still permits
removal of a triplet at that rank. The resulting full wait has one fewer
meld. The sufficient removal thresholds are five at the endpoints,
seven next to them, and nine in the interior.

For a nonnegative integer $z$ at rank $i$, set $\rho_i(z)=z$ when
$z<h_i$. For $z\ge h_i$, put

$$
\rho_i(z)=h_i+((z-h_i)\bmod3).
$$ {#eq-truncation}

Put $\tau_i(z)=(z-\rho_i(z))/3$, a nonnegative integer.
Then $0\le\rho_i(z)\le h_i+2$ and $z=\rho_i(z)+3\tau_i(z)$.
Apply these functions coordinatewise to a hand.

Let $\mathcal K_n$ be the finite set of full waits satisfying
$0\le a_i\le h_i+2$ at each rank. For $a\in\mathcal K_n$, write

$$
\begin{aligned}
\kappa(a)&=(|a|-1)/3,\\
S(a)&=\{i:a_i\ge h_i\},\\
r(a)&=|S(a)|.
\end{aligned}
$$

Every core has $\kappa(a)<5$ at order one and $\kappa(a)<8n-4$ at higher
orders. Its size is at most $\sum_i(h_i+2)$, which is $14$ at order one
and $24n-12$ for $n\ge2$, while $|a|=3\kappa(a)+1$.

::: {#thm-core}
## Unique core and tails

Every full wait has a unique expression

$$
c=a+3k,
\qquad a\in\mathcal K_n,
$$

where $k_i$ is an arbitrary nonnegative integer at each $i\in S(a)$,
and $k_i=0$ elsewhere. Conversely every such expression is a full wait.
The meld count is

$$
m=\kappa(a)+\sum_{i\in S(a)}k_i.
$$ {#eq-grade}
:::

The core in this theorem is $a_i=\rho_i(c_i)$, and its tail is
$k_i=\tau_i(c_i)$. For example, $(3,1,12)$ has core $(3,1,3)$ and tail
$(0,0,3)$: the original five melds split into two core melds and three
added triplets.

::: {.proof}

Whenever $c_i\ge h_i+3$, remove a triplet at $i$. The resulting hand remains
a full wait and has one fewer meld. Its truncation is unchanged, because
both $c_i$ and $c_i-3$ are at least $h_i$ and have the same residue modulo
three. Repeating terminates at the coordinatewise truncation, a full wait
bounded at rank $i$ by $h_i+2$. Adding the removed triplets recovers the original hand.

For uniqueness, a coordinate $a_i<h_i$ has zero tail, so $c_i=a_i<h_i$.
At a coordinate $h_i\le a_i\le h_i+2$, the residue of $c_i$ modulo three
determines $a_i$, and then $k_i=(c_i-a_i)/3$ is determined too.
Summing the coordinate identity proves @eq-grade.
:::

The local three-tile bands make the cells disjoint. Every minimal full
wait lies in this profile box, giving the upper bound
$m<8n-4$ on its meld count when $n\ge2$. A truncation core may still
contain removable melds; the decomposition provides unique cells.

## An exact finite counting formula {#sec-formula}

Let $\operatorname{MC}(r,s)$ count weak compositions of $s$ into $r$ parts:

$$
\operatorname{MC}(r,s)=
\begin{cases}
\binom{r+s-1}{s},&r\ge1,\\
1,&r=0,\ s=0,\\
0,&r=0,\ s>0.
\end{cases}
$$

::: {#thm-count}
## Counts from cores

For every natural meld count $m$, the number $F_n(m)$ equals

$$
\sum_{\substack{a\in\mathcal K_n\\\kappa(a)\le m}}
\operatorname{MC}\bigl(r(a),m-\kappa(a)\bigr).
$$
:::

For each core, @eq-grade leaves a weak composition of the remaining meld
count among its active ranks. @thm-core gives a bijection, so different
cores never count the same hand. Cores with $r(a)=0$ contribute a single
hand at $m=\kappa(a)$.

This is a finite formula at every fixed $n$. Evaluating it still requires
finding the bounded full cores. The box contains $175$ candidates at order one and
$5^2\cdot7^2\cdot9^{3n-4}$ at higher orders, so direct evaluation can be large even though that box no
longer grows with $m$.

## Rational generating series {#sec-series}

Treat the ordinary generating series formally:
$G_n(t)=\sum_{m\ge0}F_n(m)t^m$. Each active rank contributes an independent
geometric series, and @thm-count gives

$$
G_n(t)=\sum_{a\in\mathcal K_n}
\frac{t^{\kappa(a)}}{(1-t)^{r(a)}}.
$$ {#eq-series}

Since $r(a)\le3n$, this has the common denominator $(1-t)^{3n}$.
More explicitly,

$$
(1-t)^{3n}G_n(t)=P_n(t),
$$ {#eq-numerator}

where

$$
P_n(t)=\sum_{a\in\mathcal K_n}
t^{\kappa(a)}(1-t)^{3n-r(a)}.
$$

The numerator is a finite polynomial. @eq-series and @eq-numerator are
formal power-series identities, with no analytic convergence condition.

## Eventual polynomial behavior {#sec-polynomial}

The local-profile estimate gives the sufficient starting bound

$$
B_n=\begin{cases}
2,&n=1,\\
5n-4,&n\ge2.
\end{cases}
$$

::: {#thm-polynomial}
## A uniform polynomial range

There is an explicit polynomial $H_n(x)\in\mathbb Q[x]$ of degree at most
$3n-1$ such that

$$
F_n(m)=H_n(m)\qquad(m\ge B_n).
$$
:::

Use binomial coefficients as polynomials in their upper argument and set

$$
H_n(x)=\sum_{\substack{a\in\mathcal K_n\\r(a)>0}}
\binom{x-\kappa(a)+r(a)-1}{r(a)-1}.
$$

An inactive coordinate is at most $h_i-1$ and an active coordinate is
at most $h_i+2$. Write $C_n=\sum_i(h_i-1)$, which is $5$ at order one
and $15n-12$ at higher orders. Thus

$$
\begin{aligned}
|a|&\le C_n+3r(a),\\
\kappa(a)+1&\le B_n+r(a).
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-active-grade}

For $r(a)>0$, the binomial polynomial agrees with the cell count at every
integer $m\ge\kappa(a)-r(a)+1$. At $m\ge\kappa(a)$ this is the usual
weak-composition formula. At the preceding $r(a)-1$ integers it vanishes,
matching the absent core. For $r(a)=0$, the cell contributes nothing once
$m\ge B_n$, because @eq-active-grade gives $\kappa(a)<B_n$.
Thus $m\ge B_n$ suffices for every cell. Each nonzero row polynomial has
degree $r(a)-1\le3n-1$, proving @thm-polynomial. This cutoff is sufficient;
smaller starting points can result after cancellations.

The same weighted bound controls the numerator in @eq-numerator:
each summand has degree at most $\kappa(a)+3n-r(a)\le B_n+3n-1$.
Hence $\deg P_1\le4$, and $\deg P_n\le8n-5$ for $n\ge2$.

For three ranks, the [earlier exact formula](three-ranks.html) simplifies to

$$
G_1(t)=\frac{6t^2+3t^3}{(1-t)^3}.
$$

It agrees with the known coefficients
$F_1(m)=\binom{3m-2}{2}$ for $m\ge1$, and $F_1(0)=0$.

## The exact degree and leading coefficient {#sec-leading}

::: {#thm-leading}
## The fully active contribution

For every $n\ge1$, the polynomial in @thm-polynomial has degree exactly
$3n-1$ and leading coefficient

$$
\frac{3^{3n-1}}{(3n-1)!}.
$$

The numerator in @eq-numerator satisfies

$$
P_n(1)=3^{3n-1}>0.
$$
:::

A fully active core has $r(a)=3n$, so every coordinate lies in its local
band $h_i\le a_i\le h_i+2$. Proposition 6.2 of @xue-zhong-2026 makes
all such hands full-sided whenever their size is one modulo three.
Each three-tile band contains one representative of every residue class.
Thus the fully active cores are exactly the vectors in these bands whose
coordinate sum is one modulo three.

Choose residues at any $3n-1$ ranks freely. The sum condition determines
the last residue, so there are exactly $3^{3n-1}$ such cores. Each
contributes a binomial polynomial of degree $3n-1$, with leading
coefficient $1/(3n-1)!$. Every other core has fewer active ranks and
contributes smaller degree. This proves the exact degree and coefficient
without finding any lower-dimensional core table.

At $t=1$, a summand of $P_n(t)$ is one for a fully active core and zero
for every other core. The same count proves the numerator identity in
@thm-leading. In particular $1-t$ does not divide $P_n(t)$, so the
common denominator $(1-t)^{3n}$ cannot be reduced by cancellation.

## The exact polynomial starting index {#sec-start}

Let $R_n=\deg P_n$ for the actual numerator in @eq-numerator, after all
coefficient cancellations. The numerator is nonzero by @thm-leading. Put

$$
s_n=\max\{0,R_n-3n+1\}.
$$

::: {#thm-start}
## Exact starting index

The counting polynomial satisfies

$$
F_n(m)=H_n(m)\qquad(m\ge s_n).
$$

If $s_n>0$, it fails at $m=s_n-1$. More generally, a polynomial in $\mathbb Q[x]$ can give
all counts from a natural index $u$ onward if and only if $s_n\le u$.
:::

Write $P_n(t)=\sum_{j=0}^{R_n}p_jt^j$. Expanding the common denominator
gives an alternative expression for the same eventual polynomial:

$$
H_n(x)=\sum_{j=0}^{R_n}p_j
\binom{x-j+3n-1}{3n-1}.
$$

For $m\ge s_n$, every basis polynomial agrees with the corresponding
series coefficient: terms with $j>m$ are in their integer zero range.
If $R_n\ge3n$, at $m=R_n-3n$ only the final term can disagree, and

$$
\begin{aligned}
&H_n(R_n-3n)-F_n(R_n-3n)\\
&\qquad=(-1)^{3n-1}p_{R_n}\ne0.
\end{aligned}
$$

Any polynomial agreeing with the count on a tail is unique, since two
such polynomials coincide at infinitely many rational points. This proves
both the sharp boundary and the assertion about every possible counting
polynomial in @thm-start. The bound $R_n\le B_n+3n-1$ recovers $s_n\le B_n$;
a numerical improvement at a particular order reduces to determining the
actual numerator degree.

## Density among uncapped hands {#sec-density}

Let $A_n(m)$ be the number of all nonnegative multiplicity vectors on the
same $3n$ labelled ranks with total size $3m+1$. Stars and bars gives

$$
A_n(m)=\binom{3m+3n}{3n-1}.
$$ {#eq-ambient}

For $n\ge1$ this count is positive at every $m$, and full waits form a
subset of these hands. Thus $F_n(m)/A_n(m)$ is the probability of a full
wait when each multiplicity vector of that size is equally likely.

::: {#thm-density}
## Full waits have density one

For every fixed $n\ge1$,

$$
\lim_{m\to\infty}\frac{F_n(m)}{A_n(m)}=1.
$$
:::

The right side of @eq-ambient is a polynomial in $m$ of degree $3n-1$,
with leading coefficient $3^{3n-1}/(3n-1)!$. By @thm-leading, the full-wait
count agrees eventually with a polynomial having exactly the same degree
and leading coefficient. Their quotient therefore tends to one.

The sampling in @thm-density assigns equal probability to multiplicity
vectors. This specifies a multiset model with no physical copy cap.
For three ranks, the ratio for $m\ge1$ is explicitly

$$
\frac{F_1(m)}{A_1(m)}=
\frac{(3m-2)(3m-3)}{(3m+3)(3m+2)}.
$$

For example it is $1/6$ at $m=2$ and $63/88$ at $m=10$, so the limiting
statement can coexist with a substantial deficit at small meld counts.

## A six-rank diagnostic {#sec-six-ranks}

A separate ordinary computation explores how close $B_n$ is to the exact
start. For six ranks it checks the $5^2\cdot7^2\cdot9^2=99225$ candidates in the
profile box, finds 8114 full cores, and gives the candidate numerator

$$
\begin{aligned}
P_2(t)={}&8t^3+68t^4+141t^5\\
&+68t^6-17t^7-28t^8\\
&+t^9+2t^{10}.
\end{aligned}
$$

This has $P_2(1)=243$, agreeing with @thm-leading. If the computed numerator
is confirmed, @thm-start gives the exact start $10-6+1=5$.
@tbl-six-ranks compares that polynomial with direct counts of all uncapped hands of each fixed size.

The direct count at $m=4$ differs from the polynomial by two, so the
computed range cannot start earlier than five. Lean now proves the
sufficient range $m\ge5$ at this order: the highest allowed numerator
coefficient cancels, giving $\deg P_2\le10$. An exact start of five still
requires proving that the coefficient of $t^{10}$ is nonzero.

The [top-layer reduction](TopLayer.lean) isolates the highest allowed
coefficient without counting the entire core box. For each core define the
nonnegative coordinate defects

$$
\delta_i=h_i-1+3\mathbf1_{i\in I(a)}-a_i.
$$

At every $n\ge2$, its cell reaches degree $8n-5$ exactly when
$\sum_i\delta_i=2$. Consequently

$$
[t^{8n-5}]P_n(t)=
\sum_{a:\,\sum_i\delta_i=2}(-1)^{3n-r(a)}.
$$

These statements, reconstruction from the activity mask and defects, and the
weak-composition count $\binom{3n+1}{2}$ of possible defect patterns are
proved in Lean. At six ranks there are just 21 patterns and 64 masks per
pattern; an injective encoding proves that at most 1344 cores can contribute. The [small diagnostic](top-layer-check.py) checks both a greedy scan
and literal recursive meld decomposition on these 1344 assignments. For
every pattern it finds a coordinate whose activity can be toggled while
preserving full-sidedness, so the two signs cancel. Its
[output](top-layer-check.json) records the coordinate and full masks for
each pattern.

The toggle invariance is now proved in Lean. The
[canonical tail criterion](TailCriteria.lean) expresses full-sidedness above
any residue representative as linear inequalities in its triplet counts.
The [six-rank criteria](SixRankCriteria.lean) specialize this to each pair
of missing tiles, with arbitrary natural triplet counts rather than just
zero or one. For example, above $(-1,3,5,5,3,1)$ full-sidedness requires
$t_0>0$, at least one of $t_1,t_4$ positive, and at least one of $t_2,t_5$
positive; $t_3$ is irrelevant. The
[free-coordinate theorem](SixRankTop.lean) covers every deficit-two pattern,
using its representation by two possibly coincident missing tiles.
The [encoding equivalence](SixRankEncoding.lean) identifies the full
cores in this layer with the full pattern-mask codes. An inactive rank
contributes $-1$ and an active rank contributes $1$, so the product of
coordinate signs equals $(-1)^{6-r(a)}$. Toggling a free coordinate preserves
full-sidedness and reverses that product. The
[general mask cancellation](MaskCancellation.lean) pairs these terms,
and the [six-rank cancellation theorem](SixRankCancellation.lean) gives

$$
[t^{11}]P_2(t)=0,\qquad \deg P_2\le10.
$$

Hence $s_2\le5$ and $H_2(m)=F_2(m)$ for every $m\ge5$. This sufficient
range is proved without evaluating the full core table. The displayed
numerical coefficients, including the proposed nonzero coefficient of
$t^{10}$, remain computational data.


The [C++ source](six-rank-cores.cpp) compares a triplet-greedy scan,
normalized sequence templates, and literal recursive meld decomposition
on every draw case. For six ranks these are 198450 core draw cases and
1791504 further draw cases from the entire fixed-size sample spaces for
$m=0,\ldots,8$. The core formula and generating-series coefficients are
also compared through $m=40$. The three-rank run recovers the previously
proved formula. The [raw data](six-rank-cores.json) include the full
core-grade/active-rank histogram; [exact rational analysis](six-rank-summary.py)
produces the [polynomial coefficients and comparisons](six-rank-summary.json).

| $m$ | Direct full count | Polynomial value |
| ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 3 | 8 | $-5$ |
| 4 | 116 | 114 |
| 5 | 717 | 717 |
| 6 | 2790 | 2790 |

: Six-rank computational data {#tbl-six-ranks}

These six-rank cardinalities are computational evidence. The symbolic
Lean theorems above do not evaluate that finite core table.

The [next-layer formula](NextLayer.lean) works at every $n\ge2$.
Writing $q(a)=3n-r(a)$, it gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
[t^{8n-6}]P_n(t)
={}&\sum_{\delta(a)=2}q(a)(-1)^{q(a)-1}\\
&+\sum_{\delta(a)=5}(-1)^{q(a)},
\end{aligned}
$$

where $\delta(a)=\sum_i\delta_i$ and a term with $q(a)=0$ in the
first sum is zero. [Weighted mask cancellation](WeightedMasks.lean)
shows that two distinct free coordinates eliminate even the weighted
contribution. This separates the remaining optimality question into two
thin layers; their numerical contributions at six ranks are not yet certified.

## Checked Lean sources {#sec-lean}

[BoundaryTriplets.lean](BoundaryTriplets.lean) proves local removal and caps;
[TripletCore.lean](TripletCore.lean) proves the unique graded decomposition.
[TripletCounting.lean](TripletCounting.lean) gives the finite count, rational
series and polynomial evaluation, while [TripletLeading.lean](TripletLeading.lean)
proves the exact degree and leading term.
[FullWaitDensity.lean](FullWaitDensity.lean) proves density one, and
[PolynomialStart.lean](PolynomialStart.lean) proves the exact numerator-degree
criterion for the first polynomial index.

[TopLayer.lean](TopLayer.lean) reduces the highest coefficient to deficit-two
cores. [TailCriteria.lean](TailCriteria.lean) gives the canonical tail criterion;
[SixRankScan.lean](SixRankScan.lean) shares closed scan formulas across the 21
criteria in [SixRankCriteria.lean](SixRankCriteria.lean).
[SixRankTop.lean](SixRankTop.lean) proves a free coordinate for every pattern.
[SixRankEncoding.lean](SixRankEncoding.lean) identifies the full codes with full
cores. [MaskCancellation.lean](MaskCancellation.lean) and
[SixRankCancellation.lean](SixRankCancellation.lean) complete the cancellation,
degree bound ten, and sufficient six-rank range from five.

[NextLayer.lean](NextLayer.lean) proves the next-coefficient reduction, and
[WeightedMasks.lean](WeightedMasks.lean) proves weighted cancellation at two
free coordinates. These symbolic statements do not evaluate the finite core table.

These files use Lean 4.35.0 against the structural library at
[this revision](https://github.com/lunaluteus/ninegates-lean4/tree/7b379afe7f54f34c59c8abdfc8e6fa5f0bee952a).
The common [checker](check-lean.py) compiles 25 modules in a fresh
temporary directory with strict linters and audits 163 declarations
against only `propext`, `Classical.choice`, and `Quot.sound`:

```sh
uv run python examples/live-waits/check-lean.py \
  --library /path/to/ninegates-lean4
```

The [copy-cap stabilization note](copy-cap-stability.html) gives the sharp
physical cap at which live counts equal these unrestricted counts.
